criteria_results.title: Identifies TerraFreight arithmetic discrepancy ($233,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo says TerraFreight detail sums to $2,567,000 and the gap is $333,000. The criterion requires $2,667,000 and $233,000, so the figures are materially different.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Tier 1 payee count error (states 6, lists 3)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states Tier 1 is said to have 6 payees but only 3 are named.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Tier 1 subtotal does not match listed entries
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo shows $6.8M+$3.1M+$2.9M=$12.8M against the stated $12,567,000, a $233,000 variance.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Tier 2 subtotal is internally inconsistent
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags the $4,221,614 Tier 2 subtotal as a balancing figure (total minus the other tiers), not a sum of payees.

criteria_results.title: Recommends complete retotaling of the Report from detail
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo recommends getting the native transfer-level data and having Pinehurst rebuild the payee summary, and recomputes the totals from line items.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Sagebrush Marketing misclassified in Tier 2
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies Sagebrush ($1.8M), which is above the $500K threshold, as misclassified in Tier 2.

criteria_results.title: Identifies incomplete ordinary course defense analysis
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the Report analyzed only the industry prong and did no debtor-creditor (subjective) analysis.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states BAPCPA made § 547(c)(2) prongs disjunctive
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo explains that since BAPCPA the transfer need meet either (A) or (B), not both.

criteria_results.title: Notes ordinary course analysis potentially understates defenses
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo argues the opposite for TerraFreight/DataStream: it withdraws their credits and raises exposure. It does not say the incomplete analysis may understate their defenses and overstate net exposure.

criteria_results.title: Identifies non-contemporaneous transfers in § 547(c)(1) defense
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies four wires paid 8-14 days after delivery (Graystone, Clearview, Northland, Summit) totaling $485,000.

criteria_results.title: Quantifies contemporaneous exchange defense overstatement ($485K)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo quantifies the four late transfers at $485,000 as not qualifying.

criteria_results.title: Identifies $1,150,000 new value error for Vanderhoff (pre-transfer)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo treats the $1,150,000 of December shipments as only partly improper: it allows $805,000 and disallows only the $345,000 excess. It does not find the $1,150,000 uncreditable as the criterion requires.

criteria_results.title: Identifies $400,000 new value error for Vanderhoff (post-petition)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo notes the March 18 post-petition $400,000 payment but still credits the $400,000 new value in its base case. It treats disallowance only as an alternative, so it does not conclude the credit cannot be used.

criteria_results.title: Calculates corrected Vanderhoff new value ($1,650,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo computes allowable new value of $2,755,000 ($2,355,000 alternative), not about $1,650,000.

criteria_results.title: Calculates corrected Vanderhoff net exposure ($5,150,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo computes Vanderhoff net of $4,224,000 ($4,624,000 alternative), not about $5,150,000.

criteria_results.title: Identifies misapplication of earmarking doctrine to Lakeshore
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies that earmarking was misapplied to the $750,000 Lakeshore payment tied to BrightMart.

criteria_results.title: Correctly explains earmarking doctrine applies only to new lender substitution
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo explains earmarking needs a third-party (new lender) advancing funds to pay a specific creditor with no estate diminution, and that a customer's instruction does not qualify.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Gerald Hutchins $525,000 severance payment as potential insider preference
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies the $525,000 Hutchins severance (7/15/24) as an omitted one-year insider transfer.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Gerald Hutchins $175,000 consulting fee as potential insider preference
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies the $175,000 Hutchins consulting fee (9/1/24) as an omitted one-year insider transfer.

criteria_results.title: Identifies failure to flag Marcus Thibodeau insider commissions

criteria_results.title: Quantifies total insider preference exposure ($1,048,000)

criteria_results.title: Notes enforceability issues for foreign entity preference claims

criteria_results.title: Identifies Harborview premium pass-through as potential non-estate property
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo notes $980K premiums + $520K fees but says the payments were debtor property under 547(b)(1) and relies on a conduit theory. It cuts Harborview exposure to about $130,000, not about $520,000.

criteria_results.title: References broker agreement fiduciary/trust provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo cites Broker Services Agreement sections 4.2-4.3 (Premium Trust Account, fiduciary capacity, not property of Client) to support removing premiums from Harborview exposure.

criteria_results.title: Identifies incorrect statute of limitations (Report says 1 year)

criteria_results.title: States correct § 546(a)(1) deadline as March 14, 2027
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the two-year date is March 14, 2027, rolled to Monday March 15, 2027 because it is a Sunday. That is the correct two-year deadline.

criteria_results.title: Identifies outdated small transfer safe harbor threshold ($5,000 vs $7,575)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies the $5,000 threshold as outdated, with $7,575 applying for cases filed on or after April 1, 2022.

criteria_results.title: Quantifies safe harbor threshold impact ($68,240 overstatement)

criteria_results.title: Recommends requesting the underlying liquidation analysis
